RESPONDENT KSRTC Corporation,
 KSRTC Transport House,
 Central Officem, K.H.Road,
 Shanthinagar,
 Bengaluru-560027.
 SCCH-23 2 MVC. No.3652/2025  (Owner of KSRTC Bus bearing  Reg.No.KA-18-F-0720)
 (By Sri.SKR, Advocate)
 JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a RTA.

Annaiah vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105805605/
1 2.

The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that on 08.03.2025 at about 3.15 p.m, the deceased was proceeding as rider on a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-66-Q-3226 by observing all the traffic rules and regulations and when he reached near Bridge, Halehatti Cross, NH-173 road,
Sakkarayapatna, Kadur Taluk, Chikkamagaluru District,

at that time the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-18-F- 0720 driven by its driver with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and without observing any traffic rules dashed to the deceased's motorcycle.
Due to impact the deceased fell down on the road and died on the spot.
It is submitted that postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members.
The petitioners alleged that because of death of deceased the petitioners have suffered both financially and emotionally.
The accident was caused due to the sole negligence of driver of KSRTC Bus.
The respondent being the owner cum insurer of offending KSRTC bus is liable to pay compensation.
3. The respondent corporation emphatically denied rashness & negligence pleaded on the part of the driver of KSRTC bus.
On the contrary it is submitted that on the date and time of the alleged accident the KSRTC bus in question was on its schedule trip from Chikkagagaluru to Birur.
And the bus was being driven by its driver in slowly and cautiously on the left side of the road by observing all the traffic rules and regulations.

While it was so proceeding near Halehalli cross bridge, at that point of time the deceased who was proceeding on the left side of the bus, riding the same in rash and negligent manner that too without wearing helmet and talking over the mobile phone and suddenly took right turn and dashed against the left side of the body of the bus near the back wheels and caused the accident.
Hence the deceased was sole responsible for the accident and the driver of the KSRTC bus was no way responsible for the accident.
Rest of the averments of the petition are repudiated as false and baseless and it is prayed to dismiss the petitions.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 08.03.2025 at about 3.15 p.m.,
near Bridge, Halehatti cross, NH-173 road, Sakkarayapatna, Kadur Taluk,
Chikkamagalur District, due to actionable negligence of the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-18-F-0720 ?

3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation ? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
5.
The Petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 16 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.

On the other hand the respondent got examined the driver of the KSRTC bus as RW.1,
Annaiah vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105805605/
2
through him got marked Ex.R.1 to 5 documents.
6. Arguments were addressed on both sides.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order  for the following :
 REASONS 7. ISSUE NO.2:

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of the complaint the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver KSRTC Bus for the offences punishable under section's 106(1), 125(a) and 281 of BNS.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

Moreover the driver of the aforesaid KSRTC bus who was examined as RW.1 and during the course of cross examination he admitted that the accident happened on the after noon, he saw a two-wheeler going from a distance of about 40 feet.

Further he stated in his complaint that the two-wheeler was moving on the left side and he overtook the vehicle from his right side and went ahead, he was talking on the phone, his phone fell down and when he went to pick it up, it hit the back door of his bus, he fell down and had an accident.
RW.1 stated that he saw him fall down in the mirror when he went to pick up his mobile phone.
He admitted that his bus does not have a CCTV camera.
8. Further on perusal of IMV Report depicts that the KSRTC bus sustained left side front wheel back body scratched and the left side mirror damaged to the petitioner's motorcycle.
It shows that the driver of the bus dashed to the motorcycle to its right side.
Further if the driver of the KSRTC bus was coming in a normal speed then he would have certainly avoided the accident.
Viewed from any angle this Court does not find any reason to distrust the version of the petitioners herein.
When such is the case absolutely there is no impediment in considering the version of the petitioners herein.
The petitioners have successfully demonstrated there was a negligence on the part of the KSRTC bus driver.
With this observation issue No.2 is answered as 'In the Affirmative.
9. ISSUE No.1 :
The petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of his chief-examination and deposed that petitioner No.1 and 2 are the parents and petitioner No.3 is the younger sister of the deceased.
The Aadhaar cards of the petitioners and deceased and contents of the police papers reflect the aforesaid relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.

Since the evidence led by PW.1 is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, hence, I hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
Accordingly, this Tribunal answers issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
10. ISSUE NO.3 :
In this case the petitioners have claimed the compensation of Rs.50 lakhs on the death of deceased in the road traffic accident.

In order to substantiate the avocation and income,

sentences.text: absolutely no string of evidence is produced before this Tribunal.
It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) dated.05.07.2023.

entities.text: Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this Tribunal is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred in the year 2025.
Therefore, Rs.17,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.

11. So far as the age of the deceased is concerned the petitioners have produced the Aadhar card to show the age of the deceased as per Ex.P16 wherein the date of birth of deceased is shown as 01.01.1997, which indicates that he was aged (28 years 2 months 7 days) 29 years on the date of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '17'.
12.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and she died at the age of 29 years.
Therefore, in this case, 40% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Further as stated above that, as on the date of accident, deceased aged about 29 years and as such, 40% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.23,800/- p.m. (Rs.17,000 + 6,800/- i.e. 40%).
13. Further as stated above the deceased was a bachelor, as per the decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla verma V/s.

Delhi Transport Corporation, the 50% of the income of the deceased shall be deducted towards her personal expenses as the deceased unmarried, thereby the 50% income of the deceased has to be deducted for her personal expenditure.

On such deduction,
the income of the deceased comes to Rs.11,900/- p.m. (Rs.23,800 X 50/100).
14. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.11,900/- p.m. and the multiplier '17' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.24,27,600/- (Rs.11,900 X 12 X 17)

Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.24,27,600/- under the Annaiah vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105805605/
4 head of loss of dependency.
15.

Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.
Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years.

16. In this case, petitioners No.1 and 2 are the parents of deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner is entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose of their child during their lifetime.
Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their oral in the family unit.
In case where a parent has lost their minor child, or unmarried son or daughter, the parents are entitled to be awarded loss of consortium under the head of Filial Consortium.
Filial consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.
An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
Children are valued for their love and affection, and their role in the family unit.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in (2020) 9 SCC 644 in the case of the New India Assurance Company Ltd V/s Smt.Somwati & others, has held that the claims Tribunal shall award Parental and Filial Consortium in a sum of Rs.40,000/-.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Ltd V/s Smt.Somwati & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.

 2. Towards loss to estate Rs. 18,150/-
 3. Towards transportation of dead Rs. 18,150/-

ceremony expenses

 consortium to petitioner No.1 & 2  Total Rs.25,43,900/-
Less interim compensation Rs. 25,000/-

Grand Total Rs.25,18,900/-
18.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.

The Respondent being the RC owner/ internal insurer is liable and Annaiah vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105805605/
5 directed to pay the compensation amount.
Hence issue No.3 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
19. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,18,900/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 40% Petitioner No.2 - 40% Petitioner No.3 - 20%

Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 to 3 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
